answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments ensure identity integrity by binding persistent staking collateral to unique witness inputs, forcing the nadir of an attacker’s utility function well below the cost of malicious computation. We integrate a Verifiable Delay Function to thread temporal sequentiality into the sortition process, thereby preventing parallelizable identity cloning via shale-hardened hardware constraints. By imposing aggressive slashing penalties on equivocating nodes, the system reaches a robust Nash equilibrium where unforgeability remains computationally infeasible.
